No.346/2018 on the files of the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Kalpetta.
2. The petitioner is the 4th accused.
The 2nd respondent is the defacto complainant.
The offences alleged are under Sections 406, 420 and 498A read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
3. The 1st accused is the husband of the 2 nd respondent.
The 2nd and 3rd accused are the parents and the 4 th accused is the brother of the 1st accused.

4. The prosecution case is that the 2 nd respondent was subjected to cruelty, both physically and mentally, by the accused demanding more dowry and they also misappropriated the cash and gold ornaments of the 2 nd respondent.

5. I have heard Smt. Celine Joseph, the learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri. Sangeetha Raj N.
R., the learned Public Prosecutor.
There is no appearance for the 2nd respondent.

6. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the allegation in the final report, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not prima facie constitute an offence or make out any case against the petitioner.

Per contra, the learned Public Prosecutor submitted that there are materials on record to connect the petitioner with the crime and when prima facie case is made out, the jurisdiction vested with this Court under Section 482 of the Criminal Procedure Code (Cr.P.C.) cannot be invoked.

7. I went through Annexure IV complaint, Annexure I FIR, Annexure II final report as well as the statements of the witnesses recorded which form part of the final report and supplied to me by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

The ..4..
2025:KER:39187 FIR was registered on the basis of Annexure IV complaint.
In Annexure IV complaint, there is absolutely no allegation of cruelty, torture, harassment etc. by demanding more dowry against the petitioner.
All the allegations are against accused Nos.1 to 3.
The only allegation in Annexure IV against the petitioner is that he made his friends to call the 2 nd respondent over phone and made a proposal for marriage.

The said allegation is not at all sufficient to attract any of Nesamudheen vs State Of Kerala on 4 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100013422/
2 the ingredients of the offences alleged against the petitioner.

sentences.text: I have also perused the statement of the 2nd respondent and her parents recorded by the police under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.

The only allegation made against the petitioner therein is that the petitioner is the one taking all the decisions in the house and that he advised the 1 st accused to persuade the complainant to leave the house and further he directed his friends to threaten the 2nd respondent.

It is also alleged that the 2nd accused ill treated the 2 nd respondent at ..5..
2025:KER:39187
the direction of the petitioner

. 
8. The Apex Court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of Section 498A of IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes and warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them.

(See Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar (AIR 2022 SC 820)
and K.Subba Rao and others v. State of Telangana and others [(2018) 14 SCC 452]).

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar (AIR 2022 SC 820)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: K.Subba Rao and others v. State of Telangana and others [(2018) 14 SCC 452]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In K. Subba Rao (Supra), the Apex Court held that the court should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.
It was further held that the relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations, unless specific instances of their involvement in crime are made out.

In Kahkashan Kausar (supra), it was held that in the absence of any ..6..
2025:KER:39187 specific role attributed to the in-laws, it would be unjust if they are forced to go through the tribulations of trial.

It was further held that the allegations that are general and omnibus do not warrant prosecution under Section 498A of IPC.
9.
As stated already, there are no specific allegations, muchless any allegation at all against the petitioner so as to attract the ingredients of Sections 498A, 406 and 420 of IPC.
Hence, no purpose will be served in proceeding further against the petitioner.
Accordingly, all further proceedings against the petitioner alone pursuant to C. C. No.346/2018 on the files of the Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Kalpetta are hereby quashed.
The Crl. M. C. is allowed.
